sn11.19:0.3: The Worship of the Teacher (or Sakka’s Worship (2))
sn11.19:1.7: (As above down to: ) “Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, descending from the Vejayanta Palace, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation and worshipped the Blessed One.
sn11.19:1.8: Then Mātali the charioteer addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:
sn11.19:2.3: So who, O Sakka, is that spirit
sn11.19:2.4: To whom you bow in worship?’ [Sakka:
sn11.19:3.2: In this world with its devas,
sn11.19:3.4: He is the one whom I worship, Mātali.
sn11.19:4.4: These are the ones whom I worship, Mātali.
sn11.19:5.3: For the removal of lust and hatred,
sn11.19:5.5: These are the ones whom I worship, Mātali.’ [Mātali:
sn11.19:6.1: “‘Those whom you worship, my lord Sakka,
sn11.19:6.2: Are indeed the best in the world.
sn11.19:6.4: Those whom you worship, Vāsava.’ [The Blessed One:
sn11.19:7.4: The chief, climbed into his chariot.”
